E2 and E3 confirm that ball milling and SPS can produce bulk non-equilibrium alloys and that Mg content variation is being studied, but they do not provide evidence that intermetallic formation drives evolution or improves corrosion/oxidation resistance in this context. premises: Ti and Zn form stable intermetallic compounds (e.g., Ti2Zn, TiZn16) in Mg-rich systems
These intermetallic compounds act as corrosion barriers and limit corrosion front progression
High-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering can produce bulk non-equilibrium Mg-Ti-Zn alloys with refined microstructures
